discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch. Both assertions now use `should(value)`, which fails on `undefined` instead of short-circuiting. Checked by mutation: with the proto-to-host converter dropping `annotations`, the round-trip test now fails.

Good catch — the code fixtures all carried "overloaded" in the message, so the code check was not covered on its own. Added table-driven cases for each capacity code with a neutral message, plus an unknown code with a neutral message that must stay non-retryable.

Added a real-SDK case that aborts the request from inside the retry notice, while the wait is pending: the stream ends well under the backoff delay, no second fetch happens, no text is emitted, and no `sdk.error` is captured for the cancellation.

Leaving this out on purpose. Counting spawns in a unit test would mean mocking `node:child_process`, which breaks the promisified `execFile` (`.child` / `{ stdout }`), or putting a shell-script `git` wrapper on PATH, which won't work on Windows. We try not to add test-only plumbing like that. The process counts were checked against real checkpoints instead: CLI and VS Code sessions on a repo with 3,000 untracked files. main peaked at 3,051 concurrent git processes and 3,046 zombies for one comparison; this branch uses 6 git processes in total per comparison. The existing tests still cover correctness for both the tracked and the third-parent lookups.

Fixed in ac405ed: the SSH listing now runs a small POSIX sh script (folder passed as a positional argument) whose [ -d ] test follows symlinks, so a link to a folder gets the trailing slash and expands like locally; dotfiles and dangling links are still listed. The script is executed for real in project-files.test.ts against a temp folder with a linked folder and a dangling link.

I don't think this applies to marketplace skills. The exact directory/frontmatter match is enforced by `validateAgentSkillName` in `extensions/agent-plugin/agent-skill.ts`, which only runs for skills that come from an Agent Plugin package. Its docstring says Cline's own skill files intentionally stay more permissive. Skills under `~/.agents/skills` go through `createSkillsConfigDefinition` → `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown`, which uses the frontmatter name (falling back to the directory name) and keys the skill by that name, with no directory check.

You're right that the test only checked the directory, though. The `foo`/`bar` test now also loads the skills directory through `createUserInstructionConfigWatcher` and asserts the skill is registered as `bar` with its description, so it proves the installed skill actually loads and isn't just present on disk.

Valid, thanks. The fixture now uses `Number(undefined)`, so it stays alive when the variable is unset, and the test requires `signal=SIGTERM`, so a fixture that exits on its own can no longer pass it. Without the client's kill, the test now fails at the 20 s timeout.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Correct, and thanks for the precision. Registering the model only takes model *selection* off the catalog; `resolveBedrockModelId` still consults it, and with #14480 on main the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case goes out as `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in us-east-1. The test now captures the request path: the `us.*` and `global.*` cases assert they pass through unchanged (no catalog involved), and the bare case is named for what it checks, that the OpenAI shape comes out whichever profile the resolver picks. Comment and PR description narrowed accordingly.

agent feedback: The first three recovery tests cover the feature's main promises well: successful retry, truncation again, and nothing to compact. The tests from here onward mostly protect detailed telemetry behavior for listener errors, hooks, empty responses, and tool-call variants that the run loop already owns. If the telemetry contract is simplified to whether compaction/retry completed, I think these extra cases and much of their supporting implementation can be removed while preserving the important behavioral coverage.
